# Vault Secrets Store CSI provider examples

The following examples demonstrate common uses of the Vault Secrets Store CSI provider.

## File based dynamic database credentials

The following Secret Provider Class retrieves dynamic database credentials from Vault and
extracts the generated username and password. The secrets are then mounted as files in the
configured mount location.

```yaml
---
apiVersion: secrets-store.csi.x-k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: SecretProviderClass
metadata:
  name: vault-db-creds
spec:
  provider: vault
  parameters:
    roleName: 'app'
    objects: |
      - objectName: "dbUsername"
        secretPath: "database/creds/db-app"
        secretKey: "username"
      - objectName: "dbPassword"
        secretPath: "database/creds/db-app"
        secretKey: "password"
```

Next, a pod can be created to use this Secret Provider Class to populate the secrets in the pod:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
  labels:
    app: demo
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: demo
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
      labels:
        app: demo
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: app
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: my-app:1.0.0
          volumeMounts:
            - name: 'vault-db-creds'
              mountPath: '/mnt/secrets-store'
              readOnly: true
      volumes:
        - name: vault-db-creds
          csi:
            driver: 'secrets-store.csi.k8s.io'
            readOnly: true
            volumeAttributes:
              secretProviderClass: 'vault-db-creds'
```

The pod mounts a CSI volume and specifies the Secret Provider Class (`vault-db-creds`) created above.
The secrets created from that provider class are mounted to `/mnt/secrets-store`. When this pod is
created the containers will find two files containing secrets:

- `/mnt/secrets-store/dbUsername`
- `/mnt/secrets-store/dbPassword`

## Environment variable dynamic database credentials

The following Secret Provider Class retrieves dynamic database credentials from Vault and
extracts the generated username and password. The secrets are then synced to Kubernetes secrets
so that they can be mounted as environment variables in the containers.

```yaml
---
apiVersion: secrets-store.csi.x-k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: SecretProviderClass
metadata:
  name: vault-db-creds
spec:
  provider: vault
  secretObjects:
    - secretName: vault-db-creds-secret
      type: Opaque
      data:
        - objectName: dbUsername # References dbUsername below
          key: username # Key within k8s secret for this value
        - objectName: dbPassword
          key: password
  parameters:
    roleName: 'app'
    objects: |
      - objectName: "dbUsername"
        secretPath: "database/creds/db-app"
        secretKey: "username"
      - objectName: "dbPassword"
        secretPath: "database/creds/db-app"
        secretKey: "password"
```

Next, a pod can be created which uses this Secret Provider Class to populate the secrets in the pod's environment:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
  labels:
    app: demo
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: demo
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
      labels:
        app: demo
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: app
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: my-app:1.0.0
          env:
            - name: DB_USERNAME
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: vault-db-creds-secret
                  key: username
            - name: DB_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: vault-db-creds-secret
                  key: password
          volumeMounts:
            - name: 'vault-db-creds'
              mountPath: '/mnt/secrets-store'
              readOnly: true
      volumes:
        - name: vault-db-creds
          csi:
            driver: 'secrets-store.csi.k8s.io'
            readOnly: true
            volumeAttributes:
              secretProviderClass: 'vault-db-creds'
```

The pod mounts a CSI volume and specifies the Secret Provider Class (`vault-db-creds`) created above.
The secrets created from that provider class are mounted to `/mnt/secrets-store`, additionally a Kubernetes
secret called `vault-db-creds` is created and referenced in two environment variables.

## AWS IAM auth with IRSA

The following example uses the Vault [AWS auth method](/vault/docs/auth/aws) with
[IAM roles for service accounts (IRSA)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/iam-roles-for-service-accounts.html)
on Amazon EKS. The Vault Secrets Store CSI provider authenticates to Vault as the IAM role
associated with the application pod's service account.

The example has the following requirements:

- Vault Secrets Store CSI provider 1.8.0 or later.
- An EKS cluster with an
  [IAM OIDC provider](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/enable-iam-roles-for-service-accounts.html).
- A Kubernetes service account named `app` in the `default` namespace. Run the `kubectl`
  commands in this example in the `default` namespace.
- An IAM role named `app-role` with a trust policy that allows `sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`
  for `system:serviceaccount:default:app` with the `sts.amazonaws.com` audience. The role does
  not require permission policies, because Vault only verifies the identity of the caller.
- A KV v2 secrets engine mounted at `secret`, with a secret named `db` that contains a
  `password` key.
- A Vault policy named `app` that grants the `read` capability on `secret/data/db`.

Annotate the `app` service account with the IAM role ARN:

```shell-session
$ kubectl annotate serviceaccount app \
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn=arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/app-role
```

Enable the AWS auth method in Vault and create a Vault role that is bound to the IAM role:

```shell-session
$ vault auth enable aws

$ vault write auth/aws/role/app \
    auth_type=iam \
    bound_iam_principal_arn=arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/app-role \
    token_policies=app
```

By default, Vault calls `iam:GetRole` to resolve `bound_iam_principal_arn`. The Vault server
requires AWS credentials with the `iam:GetRole` permission. Refer to the
[AWS auth method](/vault/docs/auth/aws) documentation for more information.

The provider reads the IAM role annotation from the service account of the requesting pod.
The following ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding grant the provider permission to `get` service
accounts, in addition to the permissions that the Vault Helm chart grants. This example assumes
that you installed the Vault Helm chart with the release name `vault` in the `default` namespace,
as described in the [installation guide](/vault/docs/deploy/kubernetes/csi/installation). The
chart names the provider service account `<release name>-csi-provider`. If you used a different
release name or namespace, replace the `name` and `namespace` of the subject with the service
account name and namespace of your CSI provider.

Run the following command to find the service account of your CSI provider:

```shell-session
$ kubectl get serviceaccounts --all-namespaces | grep csi-provider
```

Apply the following ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding:

```yaml
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: vault-csi-provider-serviceaccount-reader
rules:
  - apiGroups: ['']
    resources: ['serviceaccounts']
    verbs: ['get']
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: vault-csi-provider-serviceaccount-reader
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: vault-csi-provider-serviceaccount-reader
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: vault-csi-provider
    namespace: default
```

The following Secret Provider Class uses the `aws` auth type to retrieve a password from Vault:

```yaml
---
apiVersion: secrets-store.csi.x-k8s.io/v1
kind: SecretProviderClass
metadata:
  name: vault-aws-creds
spec:
  provider: vault
  parameters:
    roleName: 'app'
    auth: |
      type: aws
    objects: |
      - objectName: "dbPassword"
        secretPath: "secret/data/db"
        secretKey: "password"
```

When a pod that uses the `app` service account mounts a CSI volume with the `vault-aws-creds`
Secret Provider Class, the provider writes the password to `/mnt/secrets-store/dbPassword`. Refer
to [File based dynamic database credentials](#file-based-dynamic-database-credentials) for an
example deployment.

If your AWS region is not `us-east-1`, set `aws.region` in the `auth` parameter. Then configure
the Vault AWS auth method to use the regional STS endpoint for the same region:

```shell-session
$ vault write auth/aws/config/client \
    sts_endpoint=https://sts.us-west-2.amazonaws.com \
    sts_region=us-west-2
```
